questions.question: In which year did the 86th Constitutional Amendment add the 11 th Fundamental Duty in the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2002**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act was enacted in **2002**.
 
• It introduced the **11th Fundamental Duty** under Article 51A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The 11th Fundamental Duty states: **"It shall be the duty of every citizen of India who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years."**
 
• This amendment was made to align with the insertion of Article 21A, which made the Right to Education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• The 86th Amendment emphasized the importance of education as a constitutional obligation for both the state and parents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• Originally, the Indian Constitution did not have any provisions for Fundamental Duties.
 
• They were added by the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Currently, there are **11 Fundamental Duties** listed under Article 51A of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (Article 21A)**
 
 
• Article 21A was introduced by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
 
• It makes free and compulsory education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• The Right to Education Act (RTE), 2009, was enacted to give effect to this constitutional provision.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**
 
 
• Known as the "Mini-Constitution," it introduced significant changes to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It added the concept of Fundamental Duties and expanded the scope of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
 
 
• **Other Constitutional Amendments Related to Education**
 
 
• **93rd Amendment Act, 2005:** Introduced Article 15(5) to enable reservation in educational institutions for socially and educationally backward classes.
 
• **104th Amendment Act, 2019:** Extended reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in legislatures and educational institutions.

questions.question: Emani Sankara Sastry was one of the first Carnatic maestros to use a contact microphone to harness the full potential of which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Veena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Emani Sankara Sastry, a renowned Carnatic musician, is credited with pioneering the use of a contact microphone to amplify the sound of the **Veena**.
 
• He adapted and modernized the traditional playing style of the Veena, making it more suitable for larger audiences in concert settings.
 
• Sastry's innovation enhanced the tonal clarity and projection of the Veena, especially for live performances.
 
• His efforts contributed significantly to increasing the versatility and prominence of the Veena in Carnatic music.
 
• He is remembered as a master of the Veena and for his contributions to Carnatic music, including his innovative techniques.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Veena:**

 
 
• The Veena is a traditional string instrument commonly used in Carnatic music, with a history dating back over 2,000 years.
 
• It typically consists of a large resonating body, a long fretted neck, and four main strings for melody, along with three drone strings.
 
• The Saraswati Veena is the most commonly played version in South Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Contact Microphone:**
 
 
• A contact microphone is designed to pick up vibrations directly from an object, rather than from the air.
 
• It is often used with acoustic instruments to amplify their sound without compromising tonal quality.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music:**
 
 
• Carnatic music is one of the two major traditions of Indian classical music, originating in South India.
 
• It emphasizes vocal compositions and complex melodic structures known as ragas and rhythmic patterns called talas.
 
 
 
• **Emani Sankara Sastry’s Legacy:**
 
 
• He received several awards, including the prestigious Padma Shri, for his contributions to music.
 
• He trained many students who went on to become distinguished Veena artists.

questions.question: The Nile River, located in ______________, has long been recognised as the world's longest river extending 6,695 km.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**North-Eastern Africa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Nile River is located in **North-Eastern Africa**, flowing through countries such as Egypt, Sudan, and Uganda.
 
• It is widely recognized as the **world's longest river**, spanning approximately 6,695 kilometers (4,160 miles).
 
• The Nile has two major tributaries: the **White Nile**, originating from Lake Victoria, and the **Blue Nile**, originating from Lake Tana in Ethiopia.
 
• It flows northward and empties into the Mediterranean Sea, making it unique among major world rivers.
 
• The river has historically been crucial for **agriculture, transportation, and civilization** in the region, especially for ancient Egypt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Importance in Ancient Civilization:**

 
 
• The Nile River played a central role in the development of ancient Egyptian civilization, serving as a source of water, transportation, and fertile soil for agriculture.
 
• The annual flooding of the Nile provided nutrient-rich silt, which was essential for farming in the arid region.
 
 
 
• **Hydrology:**
 
 
• The Nile is fed by its two tributaries: the White Nile (longer but with less water flow) and the Blue Nile (shorter but contributes the majority of the water volume).
 
• The river basin covers approximately 3 million square kilometers across 11 countries, making it a critical water resource.
 
 
 
• **Modern Usage:**
 
 
• The Nile River supports millions of people through irrigation, drinking water, and hydroelectric power.
 
• It remains a vital lifeline for agriculture and urban water supply in countries like Egypt and Sudan.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Challenges:**
 
 
• Climate change and upstream dam projects, such as Ethiopia's Grand Renaissance Dam, have raised concerns over water distribution and ecological impacts.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to balance the needs of the countries sharing the Nile's resources through agreements and negotiations.

questions.question: Who among the following acts as the chairman of the Planning Commission of the state?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Chief Minister** of a state acts as the chairman of the **State Planning Commission**.
 
• The State Planning Commission is responsible for **formulating state-specific development plans** in alignment with national goals.
 
• The Chief Minister holds the primary executive authority in the state and ensures coordination among various departments for implementing developmental schemes.
 
• State Planning Commissions were modeled after the erstwhile Planning Commission of India, which has now been replaced by the **NITI Aayog** at the central level.
 
• The Chief Minister’s role as chairman signifies the significance of their leadership in state development initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Planning Commission of India**

 
 
• Established in 1950, the Planning Commission was responsible for India’s **five-year plans** and socio-economic development strategies.
 
• It was replaced in 2015 by the **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India)**.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**
 
 
• NITI Aayog is a **policy think tank** of the Government of India that focuses on fostering cooperative federalism.
 
• It provides strategic and technical advice to both the central and state governments.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister**
 
 
• The Chief Minister is the head of the state government and is appointed by the Governor.
 
• They are responsible for the overall administration and development of the state.
 
 
 
• **State Planning Boards/Commissions**
 
 
• These are advisory bodies that assist in planning and implementing development initiatives at the state level.
 
• They work closely with the respective Chief Ministers and state departments.

questions.question: Which industry is considered a 'service industry'?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• The tourism industry is classified as a **service industry** because it provides intangible services such as hospitality, transportation, and entertainment to travelers.
 
• It contributes significantly to the economy by generating **employment opportunities** and revenue through both domestic and international tourism.

• The reaction involved the use of **cyanic acid** and ammonium to create ammonium cyanate, which then rearranged into urea.

• Friedrich Wöhler's experiment is considered a foundational moment in the field of organic chemistry.

• **Cyanic Acid (HOCN)**
 
 
• Cyanic acid is a simple, unstable organic acid that plays a key role in the synthesis of urea through ammonium cyanate.

• **Vitalism Theory**
 
 
• Vitalism was a scientific theory that posited that organic compounds could only be synthesized by living organisms due to a "vital force."

questions.question: The temperature at which an oil starts to burn, leading to a burnt flavour in the foods being prepared is called:

• The smoke point is the temperature at which an oil or fat begins to visibly smoke and break down, producing a burnt flavor and potentially harmful compounds.
 
• It is an important factor in cooking and frying, as heating an oil beyond its smoke point can negatively affect the taste and safety of the food.
 
• The smoke point varies depending on the type of oil or fat. For instance, refined oils generally have higher smoke points than unrefined oils.
 
• Common cooking oils and their approximate smoke points: Canola oil (~400°F/204°C), Olive oil (~375°F/190°C), and Avocado oil (~520°F/271°C).
 
• Oils with higher smoke points are suitable for high-temperature cooking methods like deep-frying, while oils with lower smoke points are better for dressings and low-heat cooking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Boiling Point:** The temperature at which a liquid turns into vapor. Unlike the smoke point, the boiling point is not a relevant factor for cooking oils.
 
• **Ignition Temperature:** The minimum temperature at which a substance catches fire without an external flame or spark. This is much higher than the smoke point.
 
• **Critical Temperature:** The temperature above which a gas cannot be liquefied, regardless of pressure. This term is not related to cooking oils.
 
• **Refined vs. Unrefined Oils:** Refining removes impurities, increasing the smoke point of oils. For example, refined coconut oil has a smoke point of ~450°F, while unrefined coconut oil smokes at ~350°F.
 
• **Health Implications:** Overheating oils beyond their smoke point can degrade nutrients and produce harmful compounds like acrolein, which is linked to respiratory and health issues.
